subject: Error in Part 5: Subscript out of bounds

messages.author: afbc8abc7ddeebc9
messages.subject: Error in Part 5: Subscript out of bounds
parts:
Dear all,

I have been using GGIR for a while, and originally processed a batch of files using version 1.9.2, but recently when processing the same batch of files with newer versions I keep running into the same issue when running g.shell.GGIR at Part 5. Here is the error message, which was produced using GGIR version 2.6.0 (included call below):

----------------
Errors and warnings for 201_left wrist_xxxxxx_2021-11-05 11-37-03.bin 09-45-53.bin.RData$message
[1] "subscript out of bounds"

$call
`[<-`(`*tmp*`, di, fi:(fi + 2), value = c("201                ",
"201_left wrist_xxxxxx_2021-11-05 11-37-03.bin.RData", "36"
))
----------------

Error was produced running this call to g.shell.GGIR:

g.shell.GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5), do.report=c(2,3,4,5),
             datadir=datadir,
             outputdir=outputdir,
             f0=c(), f1=c(), epochvalues2csv = FALSE,
             visualreport=TRUE, overwrite=FALSE,
             maxdur=60, nnights = c())

----------------
Metadata was processed for all parts up until Part 4, but then this file (as shown in the error) does not get processed in Part 5 (no corresponding data in meta/ms5.out). I've inspected the file and there are several days (>10) of valid data out of the total 48 days recorded.

When I process the file separately using a shorter 'maxdur' (e.g., 25), it does process fully. However, I would ideally need to include all the days (as there are some days near the end I would not like to exclude). I can't see any reason looking at the Part 2 output why this file specifically would cause an issue, and I've run into the same issue with a separate dataset - again where one file (that had at least several days of valid data) did not get processed fully.

Any suggestions or advice would be a huge help - thank you so much for all the work on this great package!

Best,
Katherine

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in Part 5: Subscript out of bounds
parts:
Hi Katherine,

It sounds like something in GGIR part 5 is not well equiped yet for handling very long recordings yet. Would you be able to send me:
  • Example RData file from your meta/basic output folder
  • Your call to the g.shell.GGIR() function.
With that I should be able to have a look whether this is easy to fix.

Kind regards,
Vincent


Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
